newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Malan, small firms discuss new tax rules.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Malan, small firms discuss new tax rules.

text.p: Congressional representatives of Brazil's small businesses were due to meet with Finance Minister Pedro Malan early Tuesday to hammer out mutually acceptable new tax rules for the sector, a deputy involved in the talks said.

A proposal that companies with annual turnover of up to 720,000 reais pay a flat tax rate of 7.5 percent would be discussed at the meeting, said Dep. Augusto Nardes who represents the small business sector.
Nardes, speaking on national CBN Radio, said he felt the 7.5 percent rate was too high for the smallest companies.

The deputy also said the sector was seeking to lengthen the repayment terms of debt owed by four million small companies to private and public banks. That debt is estimated to total approximately 8.0 billion reais.
The government began negotiating new tax rules for small firms after the Senate approved legislation which would have exempted them from tax altogether on turnover of up to 204,000 reais a year.
Finance Ministry officials warned the legislation, if approved in the Chamber of Deputies, would have cost about 4.0 billion reais in lost tax revenues.
